opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum £20,000 (New Projects and Commissions; Acquisitions and Collections; Long-Term Research); £5,000 (Conferences, Lectures and Publications); £2,500 (Research and Travel grants)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months) for exhibitions, commissions, acquisitions, conservation, conferences, publications and research; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for Research and Travel grants. Individuals independently wishing to develop their own practice are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions, max £20,000); Acquisitions and Collections (acquisition, conservation, cataloguing, display, max £20,000); Conferences, Lectures and Publications (max £5,000); Long-Term Research grants (max £20,000); and Research and Travel grants for individuals (max £2,500). Applications are considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open (closes 1 September 2026).

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Accommodation provided in Leeds or Hertfordshire, plus travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, rest of world up to £1,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for six-week Senior Fellowships. Projects at Studios & Gardens must relate to Henry Moore.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships allowing researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Types include Visiting Research Fellowships, Artist Research Fellowships and Senior Fellowships. Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round of fellowship applications will open in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 cash prize for MA dissertation, plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university, on a sculpture-related subject. Dissertations must not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Each year the Henry Moore Institute awards two prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture (one BA, one MA). Submissions should have a strong focus on primary/secondary sources and original research. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
